steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: A market is any opportunity for buyers and sellers to interact to establish price — physical or virtual. | Key Fact: Factor markets trade factors of production (labour market, capital market). Product markets trade finished goods and services to consumers. | Key Fact: The price mechanism allocates resources: rising prices signal shortage, attracting producers; falling prices signal surplus, driving producers away. Functions: signalling, rationing, incentivising. | Key Fact: Primary sector extracts raw materials (farming). Secondary manufactures goods (factories). Tertiary provides services (retail, finance). The UK is ~80% tertiary.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the difference between factor markets and product markets, giving an example of each. | Describe the three functions of the price mechanism in allocating resources. | Analyse why the UK economy has shifted from secondary to tertiary sector dominance.
